criteria.S1: Scope: the operative noun phrase covers more (or other) land than the instrument it rests on evidences
criteria.S2: Party: the person most affected is not a party, not the addressee, or not shown to have been served
criteria.S3: Agency: the operative effect is imposed without any act or consent of the person it binds
criteria.S4: Term shift: a key word (possession, owner, proprietor, possessions) changes meaning between documents
criteria.S5: Text gap: the operative text itself is not held; it is known only from a later recital or summary
criteria.S6: Inconsistency: dates, years or descriptions conflict between records of the same act

scale: 0 = not present on the record; 1 = present but contested or SOURCE PENDING; 2 = present on the face of a held record
timing_rule: T counts dated events within 45 days of a pre-set decisive moment (limitation date, a death, a final refusal, a demolition). An event the record itself explains (a hearing that caused it, a customary term day) scores 0. Each event is counted once.
formula: D = S x (1 + T), where S = S1+...+S6 (max 12)

docs.title: 1955 High Court possession order (Order 14), Western Ground Rents v Frederick Buckler

why.S1: Recited as covering “the whole of the farm”. The 1987 judgment records the 1916 tenancy as “of the whole of the farm” too; the wiki's case that Parcel A had left the holding by 1928 is SOURCE PENDING. Scored 1, not 2.
why.S2: Frederick Buckler alone was sued. Mary, living in the house, was not a party; the 1987 judgment records the order was not enforced against the house because of her.
why.S3: A court order against the tenant who was sued. Nothing unusual in the act itself.
why.S4: “Possession” of a farm under a tenancy is later read beside an ownership question it did not decide.
why.S5: The order, writ, affidavit and any plan are not held (EV-0032). Known only from the 1987 recital.

t.why: The yearly tenancy began on 2 February 1949, and a notice to quit a yearly tenancy has to end on the anniversary: explained.

t.event: Enforcement 4 Jul 1955, soon after Mary's leg amputation
t.why: No exact date for the operation; the record shows the house was spared because of it, which cuts against reading pressure into the timing.

docs.title: The two letters of 31 October 1974 (BP Pension Trust Ltd and BP Properties Ltd)

why.S1: BP Properties granted occupation of “the house and garden” while it had only “agreed to buy”; the conveyance came in May 1975. The Court of Appeal heard this point and rejected it as “rather technical”. Scored 1.
why.S2: Addressed to Mrs Buckler but sent to her solicitor, who received them on the morning of 4 November 1974.
why.S3: The Court of Appeal: BP Properties “neither sought nor waited for her acceptance”; she held “whether she liked it or not” as licensee.
why.S4: Her possession changes character, from adverse to licensed, by the other side's letter alone.
why.S5: Full text held: quoted in the 1987 judgment.

t.event: Letters received 4 Nov 1974; the 12 years from the possession order of 11 Dec 1962 ran out on 11 Dec 1974 (37 days later)
t.why: Partly explained: the letters answered a notice of appeal issued on 30 Oct 1974 and a stay hearing fixed for 4 Nov 1974. Their nearness to the limitation date is still on the face of the judgment.

docs.title: HM Land Registry first registration of WA240304 (farmhouse and garden), register edition 23 February 1983

why.S1: Whether the land in the 23 May 1975 conveyance was all land Western Ground Rents had held is the open question on wiki page 3191. Scored 1.
why.S2: Mary (Nancy) Williams was in actual occupation. Whether any notice reached her before her death is not yet shown; HMLR's file holds letters of 8 and 12 April 1983, after it. Scored 1 (open).
why.S3: Registration is an administrative act on an application; no agency defect is visible.
why.S4: “Registered proprietor” and “paper title” are later read as ownership in the 1987 and 1989 decisions.
why.S5: The 31 December 1969 conveyance, the recited root, is not on HMLR's disclosed schedule of 30 July 2026; form 1C and the old title plan are not yet obtained.
why.S6: The 1987 judgment dates registration of “the whole of the farm” to November 1982; the farmhouse title's register edition is 23 February 1983. HMLR's schedule lists a plan “dated 23 February 1975” for a conveyance of 23 May 1975, and an HMLR letter quotes the recited year as “One thousand One hundred and sixty nine”.

t.event: Register edition 23 Feb 1983; Mary (Nancy) Williams died 26 Mar 1983 (31 days later)
t.why: No explanation on the record. Age and health at the time are a plain alternative explanation for the death; the registration date is the registry's.

docs.title: The 1988 eviction, injunction and demolition papers

why.S1: The injunction sought covered the building only; no scope mismatch shown.
why.S2: The family were parties to the injunction application.
why.S3: A court refused relief after a hearing; no agency defect is visible.
why.S4: The press calls BP “the owners of the land”: the possession result is restated as ownership.
why.S5: Enforcement records and the injunction orders are awaited (GHF-E027-04); the ITV report carries no on-screen date.
why.S6: The Western Mail places the civil injunction hearing at “Cardiff Crown Court”; the ITV report has the High Court in Cardiff granting an earlier injunction. Which court made which order is unresolved.

t.event: Injunction refused (reported 6 Dec 1988); farmhouse demolished in the early hours of 6 Dec 1988
t.why: Same episode, so the demolition following the refusal is expected; scored because nothing was left for Strasbourg to protect.

t.event: Strasbourg registered application 14464/88 on 12 Dec 1988, 6 days after the demolition
t.why: Independent institution; no explanation for the registration date on the record.

t.event: House of Lords refused leave 3 Mar 1988; first eviction attempt 29 Apr 1988; application lodged 3 May 1988
t.why: The family's own response to the eviction attempt: explained.

docs.title: European Commission of Human Rights, application 14464/88, inadmissible 14 April 1989

why.S4: The wiki's catalogue summary: no “possession” because the courts had held the property belonged to another. A Limitation Act ruling on possession becomes a Convention finding on possessions.
why.S5: Decision text not held; the case file was reported destroyed under the Court's retention policy (EV-0122).

docs.title: Control: 1962 Cardiff County Court possession order (Mr and Mrs Frederick Buckler)

why.S4: A possession order later used to start a limitation clock.
why.S5: Order not held; known from the 1987 recital.

docs.title: Control: Court of Appeal judgment, 31 July 1987

why.S1: Appeal limited to the farmhouse and garden, stated plainly.
why.S4: Uses “paper title” and “registered proprietors” for BP.
why.S6: November 1982 registration date for the whole farm (see C).

why.S1: Her ownership through her grandfather rests on documents not yet produced.
why.S5: Typed statement held on the wiki.
